title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
content:
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
Approximately 500 US federal, state, and local government organizations now use Claude. Weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year. Those organizations run some of the most important systems in the country, usually on tight budgets and with long procurement cycles. This agreement is built to support that work, so they can apply Claude to hard problems without a large upfront commitment.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
How Claude is helping public servants get more done
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
- Utah gave Claude Code to 34 developers across 10 state agencies. 80% had a working environment within 30 minutes, 71% reported saving 20+ hours by the end of the four-week pilot.
- A US state CIO confirmed their team was able to respond to a ransomware attack in 8 minutes vs. the usual 2-3 days thanks to Claude.
- A US federal security team used Claude Mythos to detect and patch the vulnerability that would have allowed for the takeover of a critical production system in about two days. A human penetration test the month before had missed it.
- A cybersecurity professional at a major agency found and patched bugs in critical financial systems.
- A US state IT developer moved nearly 900 API methods to a new framework in two days. The project had been scoped for a month.
- A US state IT director used Claude Code to document 12 legacy code repositories, mapping 467 database tables and flagging 27 risks along the way.
- More than half of the US states, some of the largest localities, and some of the countries largest critical infrastructure operators participated in our SLTT cyber defense program.
Meeting government security requirements
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Getting started
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
For more information, contact us here.

report.summary: Anthropic expands its GSA partnership to offer a 40% Claude discount across all government levels and launches an implementation program.
report.background: Government agencies have been experimenting with generative AI, but adoption has been slowed by strict security reviews, long procurement cycles, and tight budgets. Anthropic already had a GSA relationship; this expansion aims to remove pricing and purchasing friction. The GSA Multiple Award Schedule lets agencies buy pre-negotiated products, and FedRAMP authorizations are required for sensitive unclassified work. Claude’s availability through AWS and Google Cloud gives agencies cloud-native paths to compliance. The deal comes as public-sector AI use accelerates: more agencies are testing coding assistants and cybersecurity tools, while vendors compete on federal readiness. By extending discounts to state, local, tribal and territorial governments and waiving minimum commitments, Anthropic is betting that lower barriers will convert pilots into sustained production use.
key_points: The agreement gives government buyers a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. It applies whether agencies buy directly now or through cloud providers later, and it extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments. Agencies face no minimum spend commitment and pay only for usage, with estimated savings of $1 billion.

Anthropic is launching a dedicated implementation program for public-sector agencies, borrowing best practices from its private-sector customers. The program is meant to help agencies move from pilots to production, covering deployment, adoption and governance. It will roll out in coming weeks, complementing the pricing deal rather than replacing procurement or security work.

Adoption is growing quickly. About 500 US federal, state and local organizations now use Claude. Weekly active users of Claude for Government are up roughly eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year. That growth signals demand for AI tools that meet government security requirements.

Agencies report concrete results. Utah gave Claude Code to 34 developers; 80% had a working environment within 30 minutes, and 71% saved 20+ hours in a four-week pilot. One state responded to a ransomware attack in eight minutes instead of two to three days. Other teams used Claude to patch vulnerabilities, migrate APIs and document legacy code.

Security and compliance remain central. Claude for Government reached general availability on September 30 with FedRAMP High authorization and near-parity with commercial features. Agencies can also access Claude via Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI, both FedRAMP High. Claude Enterprise is pursuing FedRAMP Moderate through the FedRAMP 20x program.
report.impact: The deal lowers a major barrier to AI adoption in government: procurement and price uncertainty. For the AI industry, it signals that public sector contracts will reward vendors with strong compliance, cloud distribution and flexible purchasing. Competitors may need to match discounts, FedRAMP coverage and implementation support. For developers, easier access through GSA, AWS and Google Cloud could mean more government projects and demand for secure, auditable AI workflows. For regular users, faster backlogs, quicker cyber incident response and modernized services could improve public services. But agencies must still manage data privacy, model risk and human oversight, especially for sensitive unclassified work.
report.tools: To follow up, watch Claude for Government and Claude Enterprise on Anthropic’s public-sector page, and Claude Code for coding pilots. Try the Claude API via Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI to see FedRAMP-aligned deployment paths. Government buyers can use GSA’s Multiple Award Schedule OneGov discount. Check the FedRAMP Marketplace for authorization status. No specific open-source project is tied to this announcement, but open-source policy and procurement communities may track the deal’s impact.
